title: The casualty-investigation reg-box on QB5_C_B#q5 cited STCW Table A-III/2, a competence standard, while ISM Code section 9 - which the card teaches in four separate layers - was absent from it
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT independent review of the Tranche 2 adjudication packet. STCW Table A-III/2 remains in the casualty-investigation REG-BOX on QB5_C_B#q5. It is the management-level competence specification for Chief Engineer and Second Engineer officers on ships of 3,000 kW propulsion power or more; it is not the governing casualty-investigation regime. The card itself teaches ISM section 9 repeatedly, but section 9 is absent from the REG-BOX. Remove the A-III/2 row and put ISM Code section 9 in that slot, without implying that section 9 is the flag-State statutory marine-safety-investigation regime.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD. The row's own description had already been narrowed by CORR-GPT-T1-QB5CB-20260904 to a self-qualifying form ending 'It is a competence standard, not an investigation provision', and that record listed the row's survival in its own report-only list. A row whose description has to explain that it does not govern the question is a row that does not belong in that box; the tranche-1 narrowing made the defect legible rather than fixing it. Meanwhile ISM section 9 is load-bearing in this card in FOUR layers - the 15-second answer, the 60-second answer, the Numbers/Regs block and the CE Oral Tip - and was absent from the reg-box entirely. The brief's caution against adding a regulation merely to preserve four rows does not bite: section 9 is already the proposition the card teaches, so the replacement adds nothing the answer does not already rest on.

authority.stcw_a_iii_2: STCW Code, Table A-III/2 - Specification of minimum standard of competence for chief engineer officers and second engineer officers on ships powered by main propulsion machinery of 3,000 kW propulsion power or more. It is a competence specification at management level. It contains no provision on the conduct, reporting or analysis of a marine casualty, and confers no investigatory function on anyone.
authority.ism_section_9: ISM Code section 9, Reports and analysis of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences. 9.1 requires the safety management system to include procedures ensuring that non-conformities, accidents and hazardous situations are reported to the Company, investigated and analysed with the objective of improving safety and pollution prevention. 9.2 requires the Company to establish procedures for the implementation of corrective action, including measures intended to prevent recurrence. This is the COMPANY limb, discharged through the Master and the Designated Person Ashore.
authority.the_distinction_the_box_must_carry: TWO INVESTIGATIONS, TWO INSTRUMENTS, AND THEY MUST NOT MERGE. The flag State's statutory MARINE SAFETY INVESTIGATION is conducted by that State's marine safety investigation Authority under the Casualty Investigation Code - in full, the Code of the International Standards and Recommended Practices for a Safety Investigation into a Marine Casualty or Marine Incident, adopted by resolution MSC.255(84). The COMPANY's own investigation and learning runs under ISM section 9. The corrected row states the company limb and then says in terms that it is NOT the flag-State investigation, naming MSC.255(84) and the row that carries it. No wording anywhere in the box implies ISM section 9 governs the flag-State marine safety investigation.
authority.why_this_is_a_replacement_and_not_an_add: The brief warned against adding a regulation simply to preserve four rows. That warning is honoured by the fact that the replacement is justified independently: section 9 is cited by the card in four layers and was missing from the only block that names the card's governing instruments. The box would have been wrong to omit it even if A-III/2 had never been there.
